_comment: Candidate fields that are not (yet) in the OTE core. Each entry has a RECOMMENDED SHAPE so early adopters converge, and an observedAdoption count written by scripts/scan-extensions.mjs (never by hand) from the registered adopter feeds. A field graduates to the core through a normal proposal once its graduationQuestion is answered — see CONTRIBUTING.md. The public page renders from this file: https://opentechevents.org/extensions/
generatedNote: observedAdoption is machine-written. Everything else is maintained by hand.

extensions.name: sponsors
extensions.purpose: Who sponsors the event, as a list — distinct from organizers (who runs it) and speakers (who is on stage).
extensions.shape: array of { name, url?, tier? } — same 'a name and where to find them' discipline as organizers
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do ≥3 producers emit it, and with what shape (flat list vs. tiered)?

extensions.name: capacity
extensions.purpose: Maximum number of attendees. Not 'seats left' — that is ticketing state a nightly file cannot hold.
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do ≥3 producers emit a stable capacity (not a live seats-left counter)?

extensions.name: level
extensions.purpose: Who the event is pitched at — 'is it for me?', the axis eligibility does NOT cover (that is 'will they let me in?').
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do real conferences emit a filterable level, or only free-text audience prose?

extensions.name: speakers[].affiliation
extensions.purpose: The speaker's organisation, as ONE display name.
extensions.shape: string — a proper noun, written once, not translated (like organizers[].name / a locality's spelling)
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do ≥3 producers emit it? Lowest cost of the speakers enrichment set — no translation — so likely first to graduate.

extensions.name: speakers[].jobTitle
extensions.shape: string — free text, in the document's textLanguage; graduation needs a local translations map (D010/D023/D030)
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do ≥3 producers emit it, AND is it worth the translations-map cost?

extensions.name: speakers[].bio
extensions.purpose: A short paragraph about the speaker.
extensions.shape: string — free text prose, in the document's textLanguage; same translation cost as jobTitle, larger
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do ≥3 producers emit it structured, rather than only on the speaker's own page?

extensions.name: speakers[].image
extensions.shape: SAME shape as event image[] — a string or { url, alt, translations }. Its translations map is NOT core-validated as an extension.
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do ≥3 producers emit it, AND is it worth reopening the image[].alt accessibility apparatus nested inside speakers[]?

extensions.name: sameAs
extensions.purpose: URLs the publisher asserts describe the SAME event — the organiser's canonical page, another OTE id — for cross-aggregator deduplication. A publisher ASSERTION, not a consumer heuristic.
extensions.shape: array of HTTP(S) IRIs, uniqueItems, no userinfo — maps to schema.org Event.sameAs. Distinct from id (per-publisher stable identifier) and source.url (provenance).
extensions.graduationQuestion: Do ≥2 aggregators emit it pointing at a shared canonical URL? And does the 'deduplication across sources' non-goal need revisiting, or does 'publisher hint ≠ heuristic' hold?
